schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
schemes.description: An initiative by the Government of India that provides up to ₹6,000 per year in three equal installments as minimum income support to all small and marginal landholding farmer families.
schemes.eligibility: Small and marginal farmers holding cultivable land in their names. Excludes institutional landowners and taxpayers.
schemes.benefits: Direct financial assistance of ₹6,000 per annum, paid directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
schemes.description: A government-sponsored crop insurance scheme that integrates multiple stakeholders to protect farmers from crop losses due to natural calamities, pests, or diseases.
schemes.eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers.
schemes.benefits: Low premium rates (1.5% to 2% for foodgrains, 5% for commercial/horticultural crops) with full claim payouts for crop damage.

schemes.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
schemes.description: Under this scheme, the government issues Soil Health Cards to farmers. These cards contain crop-wise recommendations of nutrients and fertilizers required for individual farms.
schemes.benefits: Free soil testing and customized recommendations for N-P-K and micro-nutrients to reduce fertilizer expenses and improve yields.

schemes.name: PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) - Per Drop More Crop
schemes.description: Focuses on micro-irrigation technologies (drip and sprinkler systems) to promote water-use efficiency and boost crop productivity.
schemes.eligibility: Farmers having land ownership, cooperative members, or registered self-help groups.
schemes.benefits: Subsidies ranging from 45% to 55% for installing drip and sprinkler systems.

schemes.name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
schemes.description: Promotes agricultural mechanization by providing subsidies for buying modern machinery like tractors, rotavators, power tillers, and laser land levelers.
schemes.eligibility: Individual farmers, self-help groups, and cooperative farming societies.
schemes.benefits: Financial assistance (40% to 50% subsidy) on purchase of certified farm implements and custom hiring centers.

schemes.name: Mukhyamantri Kisan Kalyan Yojana (MP)
schemes.description: State-specific initiative in Madhya Pradesh that supplements the PM-KISAN scheme, providing extra financial support to farmers.
schemes.eligibility: Beneficiaries of PM-KISAN who reside in Madhya Pradesh.
schemes.benefits: An additional financial assistance of ₹4,000 per year, raising total direct benefit to ₹10,000.

mandiprices.trendReasoning: Due to high demand and lower international reserves, prices are expected to rise by 3-5% next month.
High quality Sharbati variety in Indore continues to command a premium with rising festive season demand.
Steady production and ample government buffer stocks will likely keep paddy prices stable.
Excellent monsoon in cotton belts has raised yield estimates, leading to minor downward correction in prices.

Delayed planting of late kharif crop due to rainfall gap will tighten the supply in early spring.

pestalerts.description: A destructive pest feeding on leaves, stems, and reproductive parts of maize crops. Rapid infestation spreads across hot, humid climates.
pestalerts.symptoms: Ragged leaves with large, irregular holes, light green to brown stripes on caterpillars, and visible moist sawdust-like excrement inside whorls.
pestalerts.controlMeasures: Handpick and destroy egg masses. Apply Neem oil 1500 ppm at early stages. For severe infestations, spray Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG at 0.4 g/liter of water.

pestalerts.description: A major cotton pest where larvae tunnel into bolls to feed on seeds, staining the lint and reducing market value.
pestalerts.symptoms: Rosette flowers, immature opening of cotton bolls, tiny entry holes on bolls that heal rapidly, and damaged seed cavities.
pestalerts.controlMeasures: Install pheromone traps (5-10 traps per acre). Spray Azadirachtin (Neem seed kernel extract) 5%. Spray Profenofos 50 EC (2 ml/liter) if traps show pest threshold exceedance.

pestalerts.description: Fungal disease triggered by high nitrogen fertilizer use, cool nights, and leafy dew.
pestalerts.symptoms: Spindle-shaped, diamond lesions on leaves with gray centers and brown borders. Collapsed stems (neck blast).
pestalerts.controlMeasures: Avoid excessive nitrogen application. Maintain standing water in fields. Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP at 0.6 g/liter of water.

pestalerts.description: Devastating water-mold disease that strikes during cool, damp fog conditions.
pestalerts.symptoms: Dark, water-soaked patches on leaf tips turning black, with white mildew growth on the underside under humid conditions. Rotting tubers.
pestalerts.controlMeasures: Use certified disease-free seed tubers. Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (2 g/liter) as a protective measure, or Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP if infection starts.

fertilizersToApply.name: Urea (46% N)
fertilizersToApply.timing: Apply in 2 split doses: 50% at sowing, 50% at tillering (30 days post sowing)

fertilizersToApply.name: DAP (Diammonium Phosphate - 18% N, 46% P)
fertilizersToApply.timing: Apply 100% basal dose during soil preparation / before sowing
fertilizersToApply.method: Band placement next to seed furrows

fertilizerrecommendations.organicAlternatives: Incorporate 5-10 tons of well-rotted farmyard manure (FYM) or Vermicompost per acre during plowing. Apply Azotobacter biofertilizer (seed treatment) to increase N availability naturally, and Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria (PSB) to dissolve bound soil phosphorus.

recommendations.explanation: Wheat requires cool growing conditions and mild winters. Clay-loam soils are ideal for deep root growth.
recommendations.irrigationGuide: Requires 4-6 crown root initiation (CRI) waterings. Crucial watering at jointing and milking stages.
recommendations.fertilizerGuide: NPK 120:60:40 kg/hectare. Apply phosphorus and potash at sowing.

recommendations.explanation: Mustard grows well in light sandy loam soils during winter, requiring less moisture than wheat.
recommendations.irrigationGuide: Highly drought resistant. Requires only 2 irrigations: one at pre-flowering and one at pod filling.
recommendations.fertilizerGuide: NPK 80:40:40 kg/hectare. Sulfur addition (40 kg/ha) is critical to raise seed oil content.

diseasereports.symptoms: Elongated, spindle-shaped lesions with grayish centers and dark brown borders appear on leaves, turning into node necrosis and broken panicles (neck blast).
diseasereports.treatment: Drain field water temporarily if nitrogen level is high. Apply protective spray.
diseasereports.organicSolution: Foliar spray with Pseudomonas fluorescens formulation (5g/liter) or cow-urine extracts.
diseasereports.chemicalSolution: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP (0.6g/liter) or Carbendazim 50% WP (1g/liter) at early symptom emergence.
diseasereports.prevention: Avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen. Maintain optimal plant spacing. Burn crop stubble post-harvest to kill spores.

diseasereports.symptoms: Leaves curl upward and inward, resembling cups. Foliage exhibits puckering, yellowing between veins, stunted plant growth, and drop in flower count.
diseasereports.treatment: Uproot and destroy infected plants immediately to prevent further viral transmission. Deploy yellow sticky traps.
diseasereports.organicSolution: Spray Neem oil (5ml per liter of water) mixed with a mild soap solution. Introduce natural predators like lacewings to hunt insect vectors (whiteflies).
diseasereports.chemicalSolution: Apply Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (0.5 ml/liter) or Acetamiprid 20% SP (0.2 g/liter) to eliminate the whitefly vector.
diseasereports.prevention: Cover nursery beds with fine nylon nets. Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops. Eliminate weed hosts.
